stem.text: Let h be a continuous function with \( \int_{2}^{9} h(x)\,dx = 15 \) and \( \int_{6}^{9} h(x)\,dx = 5 \). Find the value of \( \int_{6}^{2} \left(4h(x) + 1\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the requested integral and use linearity: \( \int_{6}^{2} \left(4h(x) + 1\right) dx = -(4) \int_{2}^{6} h(x)\,dx + (1)(2 - 6) \), and the constant contributes \( -4 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, the requested integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.B: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral from 2 to 6 as 5 - (15)
distractor_derivations.D: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
